features.name: Decks and subdecks
features.description: Create, rename, delete and nest decks (parent::child). The deck list shows new, learning and due counts for each deck, and parent decks roll up their children's counts.
features.reason: Decks are the main organising unit. Every study and stats action is scoped to one.

features.name: Note editor with fields and tags
features.description: Add or edit a note with Front and Back fields plus free-form tags shown as removable chips. A formatting bar offers bold, italic, underline, clear formatting, a preview toggle and an HTML source toggle. Up and down arrows move between fields.
features.reason: Creating cards on the device is shown in the screenshots. It is essential for a standalone app with no desktop companion.

features.name: Note types: Basic, Basic+Reverse, Cloze
features.description: Built-in note types generate one or more cards per note. Basic makes Front to Back. Reverse also makes Back to Front. Cloze makes one card per {{c1::...}} deletion and hides that span on the question side.
features.reason: Cloze deletions are highlighted in the listing as a headline capability.

features.name: Sticky fields
features.description: A per-field pin toggle in Add mode that keeps a field's content after saving, so the next note starts with it prefilled.
features.reason: Its absence is called out in a 1-star review, and it is cheap to build.

features.name: Media: camera, photo library and voice recording
features.description: Insert images from the camera or photo library and record audio clips with the mic into a field. Media is stored in the app container, and audio plays automatically or by tapping during review.
features.reason: Shown in the editor toolbar. Works fully offline with on-device storage.

features.name: Math rendering (MathJax/LaTeX)
features.description: Render inline and display math written as \( \) and \[ \] in card HTML, using a MathJax bundle that ships inside the app and renders in a WKWebView.
features.reason: Important for STEM users. It works offline only if the renderer is bundled, which adds some complexity.

features.name: Spaced repetition scheduler (SM-2)
features.description: Cards move through New, Learning, Review and Relearning states. Learning steps are configurable (for example 1m, 10m). Each rating updates the card's ease factor and interval, and every answer button shows the next interval it would set (for example 1m Again, 10m Good, 4d Easy). Daily new and review limits apply per deck, and the day rolls over at a configurable hour.
features.reason: This is the heart of the product: review cards just before you would forget them.

features.name: FSRS scheduler option
features.description: An alternative scheduler that models memory stability and difficulty per card, with a desired-retention setting. Its parameters are optimised on the device from the user's review history.
features.reason: The listing mentions it. It is advanced, and SM-2 is enough for a first version.

features.name: Review screen with answer buttons
features.description: Shows the question, then reveals the answer on tap. Buttons below rate the recall as Again, Hard, Good or Easy. The bottom bar shows the remaining New, Learning and Review counts in blue, red and green.
features.reason: This is the primary daily interaction.

features.name: Configurable tap zones and swipes
features.description: The user maps screen regions (top, middle, bottom, left, right) and swipe directions to actions such as show answer, rate, undo, replay audio or open tools.
features.reason: The listing calls this out for efficient one-handed study. A sensible default mapping is enough at launch.

features.name: Tools overlay
features.description: A bottom sheet of frequent actions: Undo, Study Options, Custom Study, Deck Statistics, Card Info, Filter/Cram, Scratchpad, Night Mode, Top Bar, Flag, Bury Note and Suspend Card. It also has a text size stepper, for example 1.1x.
features.reason: This is how card management actions are reached during a review.

features.name: Undo
features.description: Reverts the last answer or the last bury, suspend or flag action, including its scheduling changes.
features.reason: Mis-taps are common on mobile.

features.name: Bury, suspend and flag
features.description: Bury hides a card or note until tomorrow. Suspend removes a card from review until it is unsuspended. Flags offer seven colours that can be searched.
features.reason: These are standard card management tools exposed in the overlay.

features.name: Scratchpad
features.description: A transparent drawing layer over the card for working out answers with a finger or Apple Pencil. It has clear and undo, and a setting to turn off pressure sensitivity.
features.reason: Shown in the overlay, and one review explicitly asks for the pressure toggle.

features.name: Study timer display
features.description: An optional on-screen timer showing time spent on the current card and on the session.
features.reason: A review complains that it is missing. It is trivial to add.

features.name: Card scroll position setting
features.description: When a long card appears, it opens scrolled to the top. An option jumps to the answer separator instead.
features.reason: A review reports that automatic scrolling to the middle broke an existing workflow.

features.name: Night mode and text scaling
features.description: A dark theme for cards and the interface that follows the system or can be overridden, plus an adjustable card zoom.
features.reason: Shown in the screenshots. It costs almost nothing with SwiftUI.

features.name: Search / browser
features.description: Find notes and cards with a query syntax: words, tag:, deck:, is:due/new/suspended, flag:N, rated:N, added:N and negation with -. Results appear in a list where cards can be edited, deleted, moved to another deck, retagged, suspended or rescheduled.
features.reason: The listing highlights powerful search, and editing existing cards depends on it.

features.name: Filtered / custom study decks
features.description: Build a temporary deck from a search query with a limit and an order, for example to cram or to review cards forgotten today. Cards return to their home deck when it is emptied.
features.reason: A powerful feature, but it is built on top of search and the scheduler.

features.name: Statistics
features.description: Card counts by state (New, Young, Mature, Suspended, Buried) shown as a bar with percentages. A yearly calendar heatmap shows reviews per day. A Future Due chart shows forecast reviews over 1 month, 3 months, 1 year or all, with a cumulative line. Each view can be scoped to the deck or the whole collection, and to the last 12 months or all history.
features.reason: Shown in the screenshots. Everything is computed locally from the review log.

features.name: Deck options presets
features.description: Per-deck settings for new cards per day, maximum reviews per day, learning steps, relearning steps, graduating interval, easy interval, starting ease, maximum interval, bury siblings and new card order.
features.reason: Needed for the scheduler to be useful. Keep it to a short, clearly labelled list to avoid the reported confusion.

features.name: Import/export files
features.description: Import CSV and Anki-compatible .apkg packages from the Files app or AirDrop. Export a deck, with optional scheduling data, to a file through the share sheet. This also covers sending a deck to a friend.
features.reason: Reviews ask for deck sharing and say importing is confusing. File-based import and export stays entirely on the device.

features.name: Local study reminders
features.description: An optional daily local notification at a user-chosen time when cards are due.
features.reason: Common in flashcard apps and needs no server.

features.name: Home screen widget
features.description: A WidgetKit widget showing today's due count and a small review heatmap, reading from a shared app group container.
features.reason: Explicitly requested in a review. It runs entirely on the device.

features.name: Image occlusion editor
features.description: Draw rectangles over an image to create one card per hidden region.
features.reason: A review requests it on mobile. It is complex but needs no network.

features.name: Localization (including Italian)
features.description: Fully localized interface strings with an in-app language that follows the system setting.
features.reason: Many reviews request Italian, and one reports getting stuck in the wrong language.

features.name: Cloud sync with a server account
features.description: Synchronize the collection across devices and desktop through an online account.
features.reason: Requires an account and a server.

features.name: Download shared decks
features.description: Browse and download community decks from an online catalogue.
features.reason: Requires network access and a server.

features.name: AI card generation
features.description: Generate flashcards automatically from text using an AI service.
features.reason: Requires network access to a third-party service.

features.name: Add-ons / plugins
features.description: Third-party code extensions to the app.
features.reason: Not feasible on iOS, and the paid app does not support them either.

features.name: Custom note type and template editing
features.description: Create note types with custom fields and HTML/CSS card templates.
features.reason: Power-user feature. The built-in types cover most needs at launch.

screens.name: Deck List
screens.purpose: Home screen listing all decks with today's counts and entry points to everything else.
elements: Hierarchical deck rows with new, learning and due counts
Swipe actions: rename, options, delete, export

screens.name: Study / Review
screens.purpose: Show one card at a time and collect a recall rating.
elements: Top bar with Decks, Add, Edit and Find
Card content in a web view (HTML, images, audio, math)
Answer buttons Again, Hard, Good, Easy with next-interval labels
Remaining counts New, Learning and Review in colour
Gear button opening the tools overlay

screens.name: Tools Overlay
screens.purpose: Quick access to study actions and display settings without leaving the review.
elements: Frequent actions grid: Undo, Study Options, Custom Study, Deck Statistics, Card Info, Filter/Cram, Scratchpad, Night Mode, Top Bar, Flag, Bury Note, Suspend Card

screens.name: Note Editor
screens.purpose: Add a new note or edit an existing one.
elements: Formatting toolbar: bold, italic, underline, clear formatting, record audio, camera/photo, preview, HTML source
Field text areas (Front, Back or Text, Extra)
Field navigation arrows above the keyboard

screens.name: Browse / Find
screens.purpose: Search and manage existing notes and cards.
elements: Result list with sort field, deck and due date
Bulk actions: move deck, add or remove tags, suspend, flag, delete, reschedule

screens.name: Statistics
screens.purpose: Visualize progress and the upcoming workload.
elements: Scope toggle: deck or collection, with a search box
Range toggle: last 12 months or all history
Card Counts stacked bar and table
Future Due bar chart with cumulative line and range options
Reviews per day and answer button breakdown

screens.name: Deck Options
screens.purpose: Configure scheduling for a deck or preset.
elements: Scheduler choice SM-2/FSRS with desired retention

screens.name: Custom Study / Filtered Deck
screens.purpose: Create a temporary study session from a query.
elements: Preset options: review forgotten, study ahead, more new cards, by tag

screens.name: Card Info
screens.purpose: Show scheduling details for the current card.

screens.name: Import / Export
screens.purpose: Move decks in and out of the app via files.
elements: CSV field mapping and deck/tag selection

flows.name: First launch
steps: App opens on the Deck List with a Default deck and an optional sample deck
An empty state offers Add note or Import file
No sign-in prompt is shown

flows.name: Add a basic card
steps: Tap Add from the Deck List or review top bar
Choose note type Basic and a deck
Type Front and Back, optionally pin a field as sticky
Add tags as chips
Tap Add; the fields clear except sticky ones and a confirmation toast appears

flows.name: Add a cloze card
steps: Pick the Cloze note type
Type a sentence, select a span and tap the cloze button to wrap it as c1 (or c2 for the next one)
Optionally fill Extra
Save; one card is generated per cloze number

flows.name: Add media to a card
steps: In the editor, tap the camera icon and choose Take Photo or Photo Library
Or tap the mic icon, record, then stop and save
The media file is copied into the app container and its reference is inserted into the field
Tap the preview icon to check rendering

flows.name: Daily study session
steps: Tap a deck with due cards
The question is shown
Tap to show the answer
Rate Again, Hard, Good or Easy using a button or tap zone
The scheduler updates the card and writes a review log
Repeat until the counts reach zero, then show a congratulations screen with the next due time

flows.name: Manage a card during review
steps: Tap the gear to open the tools overlay
Choose Bury, Suspend, Flag, Card Info or Edit
Choose Undo to revert the last action if needed

flows.name: Search and cram
steps: Open Find
Enter a query such as tag:priority rated:10 -word
Review and bulk-edit the results
Tap Create Filtered Deck, set a limit and order
Study the filtered deck; empty it to return cards to their home decks

flows.name: View statistics
steps: Open Deck Statistics from the overlay or the deck menu
Toggle between deck and collection, and between 12 months and all history
Browse the calendar by year and switch the Future Due range

flows.name: Import a deck
steps: Tap Import or open a .apkg or .csv file from Files or AirDrop
For CSV, map columns to fields and choose a deck and tags
Confirm, then show a summary of notes added and duplicates skipped

flows.name: Share a deck with a friend
steps: Swipe a deck and tap Export
Choose whether to include scheduling and media
The app creates the package file
The share sheet opens for AirDrop, Messages or Files

data_model.storage: SwiftData (or SQLite via GRDB for 100k+ card performance) in the app container. Media files go in Application Support/media and are rendered in WKWebView through a local file base URL. MathJax is bundled in the app. An app group container holds widget data. Nothing leaves the device except files the user exports through the share sheet.

monetization.model: Free: no ads, no in-app purchases, no subscription, no account
monetization.notes: The original is a one-time 29.99 € purchase that funds its desktop sibling. Many low-star reviews object to that price for an app that lags other platforms and is not localized. The free remake should ship the full feature set with no limits, keep everything offline, and replace cloud sync and shared-deck download with file import and export.

user_pains.pain: Price feels too high for what the iOS app offers
user_pains.evidence: Reviews call it costly or a scam, say 20–29 € is too much for an incomplete app, and argue it is pricey without deck sharing.

user_pains.pain: Missing features available on other platforms (sticky fields, image occlusion creation, add-ons, study timer)
user_pains.evidence: Reviewers say the iPhone version is behind Android, that sticky fields are missing, that image occlusion needs a desktop extension, that plugins are absent, and that the timer is not visible.
Several reviews ask for an Italian interface and note it is the only language missing.

user_pains.pain: Confusing interface and too many unclear settings
user_pains.evidence: Reviewers describe the app as messy and hard to use, with too many settings that are unclear or poorly translated.

user_pains.pain: Hard to import or share decks without a computer
user_pains.evidence: Reviewers cannot work out how to import, want to send a deck to a friend, and complain that shared decks must go through desktop and sync first.

user_pains.pain: Weak iPad experience and no widget
user_pains.evidence: A reviewer says the app does too little on an iPad with a keyboard and asks for a widget with the study calendar.

user_pains.pain: No pressure-sensitivity toggle in the scratchpad
user_pains.evidence: A reviewer asks to disable Apple Pencil pressure when drawing.

user_pains.pain: Long cards auto-scroll to the middle
user_pains.evidence: A reviewer says new cards open mid-card instead of at the top, with no setting to change it.
A reviewer reports the app switched to Russian and could not be changed back.
An old review complains a website opened every couple of cards.
A reviewer says the missing customer support makes the app less appealing.
A reviewer wants AI generation instead of using a separate chatbot.
